title: Replace DSL Derive Directory Walk with Schema Index
description: Replace the DSL derive recursive directory walk with a generated, file-tracked schema index so rustc checksum-freshness no longer hashes directories. During cold builds rustc logs tens of thousands of ERROR rustc_interface::passes failed to compute checksum, omitting it from dep-info <dir> Is a directory (os error 21). Cause: the compile-time resource observer read_dir in framework/modules/process/artifacts/native-build/resources/compiler calls proc_macro::tracked::path on every directory it lists; the only caller is the DSL derive $id document index which recursively walks the whole plugin/module root for every #[derive(MutationLeaf)] (59 crates, ~14.8k directories). .cargo/config.toml enables checksum-freshness, so rustc fails to hash directories. Directory tracking is currently the only new-file freshness signal, so simply deleting it risks stale builds. Clean fix: replace the per-derive recursive walk with a generated, file-tracked schema index (schema-first, generated by the owning script.ts, registered in nx/launch.json), so the derive reads one tracked index file and no directories are tracked; remove directory tracking afterwards. Verify with a cold cargo build of one stdio artifact crate and one flow extension: zero EISDIR lines, and adding a new schema file triggers a rebuild.
summary: MutationLeaf now reads one generated schema document index instead of walking directories, and compiler read_dir no longer tracks those directories. Cold builds of semio-s-artifact-stdio-txt and semio-s-plugin-flow-extension-brep logged zero directory checksum errors, and adding a schema file rebuilt the stdio crates after generate-schema-index.
